procedure_steps.detail: Contact Home Energy Scotland for advice and to check funding

eligibility.income_note: Grant-and-loan scheme (Home Energy Scotland Grant and Loan): heat pump/insulation grants up to £7,500/£9,000 rural uplift; Warmer Homes Scotland element is means-tested for the fuel-poor. Income rules vary by component.

programmes.source_snippet: Home Energy Scotland offers free advice and grant or interest-free loan funding from the Scottish Government to help make homes warmer and cheaper to heat.

programmes.amount_note: HC2 certificate gives full help with NHS costs (prescriptions, dental, sight tests, travel); HC3 gives partial help; certificate usually valid for up to a year

procedure_steps.detail: Complete form HC1 (online or paper) and send it to NHSBSA

documents_required.doc: Details of income, savings and household costs

eligibility.income_note: Compares weekly income with calculated 'requirements' (personal allowances plus housing costs): full help (HC2) if income does not exceed requirements; partial help (HC3) above that. Capital limit £16,000 (£23,250 for permanent care-home residents). No single annual ceiling — it depends on household size and housing costs.

programmes.source_snippet: The NHS Low Income Scheme can help you pay for NHS prescription charges, dental treatment, sight tests, wigs and fabric supports, and travel to receive NHS treatment.

programmes.name_en: Free NHS Prescriptions and Medical Exemptions (England)
programmes.amount_note: Free NHS prescriptions for people aged 60+, under 16 (or under 19 in full-time education), pregnant or with a new baby, with certain medical conditions (medical exemption certificate), or on qualifying benefits

eligibility.income_note: Free for under-16s, 16-18 in full-time education, 60+, MatEx/MedEx certificate holders, and recipients of Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit, or UC below the earnings criteria; HC2 via the NHS Low Income Scheme.

programmes.source_snippet: You can get free NHS prescriptions if, at the time the prescription is dispensed, you are 60 or over, under 16 (or 16-18 and in full-time education), pregnant or have had a baby in the previous 12 months, or hold a valid exemption certificate.

programmes.name_local: Free NHS prescriptions (Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland)
programmes.name_en: Free NHS Prescriptions for All (Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland)
programmes.amount_note: All NHS prescriptions are dispensed free of charge in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
programmes.source_snippet: Prescription charges have been abolished in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, so all NHS prescriptions are free to everyone registered with a GP there.

programmes.name_local: Free NHS eye tests and optical vouchers
programmes.name_en: Free NHS Eye Tests and Optical Vouchers
programmes.amount_note: Free NHS sight tests and vouchers towards glasses or contact lenses for children, over-60s, people on qualifying benefits and those with certain eye conditions

eligibility.income_note: Free NHS sight test for under-16s, 16-18 in FTE, 60+, diagnosed diabetes/glaucoma and risk groups, and recipients of Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit, UC (earnings criteria) or HC2; in Scotland all residents get free NHS eye examinations.

programmes.source_snippet: You may be entitled to a free NHS sight test and an optical voucher to help with the cost of glasses or contact lenses depending on your age, benefits or medical circumstances.

programmes.amount_note: Refund of reasonable travel costs to hospital or other NHS premises for appointments, for people on qualifying benefits or the NHS Low Income Scheme

procedure_steps.detail: Claim at the hospital cashier's office with proof of benefit and travel tickets

documents_required.doc: Proof of qualifying benefit or HC2/HC3 certificate
Travel receipts/tickets

eligibility.income_note: Refund of travel to NHS treatment for recipients of Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit, UC within the earnings criteria, or HC2/HC3 certificate holders.

programmes.source_snippet: Under the Healthcare Travel Costs Scheme you can claim back reasonable travel costs to NHS appointments if you receive a qualifying benefit or hold an HC2 or HC3 certificate.

programmes.amount_note: Free NHS dental treatment for under-18s (under-19 in full-time education), pregnant women and new mothers, and people on qualifying benefits or HC2 certificates

eligibility.income_note: Free for under-18s (under-19 in FTE), pregnant women and new mothers (12 months), hospital dental patients, and recipients of Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit, or UC with take-home pay under £435/month (£935 with child element or LCW) in the last assessment period.

programmes.source_snippet: You're entitled to free NHS dental treatment if you're under 18 (or under 19 in qualifying full-time education), pregnant or have had a baby in the last 12 months, or you get certain benefits.

programmes.amount_note: Parking concessions for disabled people and those with hidden disabilities; badge costs £10 in England (up to £20 in Scotland, free in Wales) and usually lasts 3 years

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and apply online via GOV.UK (application goes to your council)
Upload photo, proof of identity, address and benefit/condition evidence
Pay the fee when approved; badge posted to you

documents_required.doc: Recent passport-style photo
Proof of identity and address
Proof of qualifying benefit (e.g. PIP award letter) or medical evidence

eligibility.income_note: Automatic eligibility for certain benefits (e.g. higher-rate DLA mobility, PIP with 8+ moving-around points, registered blind); others qualify via assessment

programmes.source_snippet: The Blue Badge scheme helps disabled people with severe mobility problems to access goods and services by allowing them to park close to their destination; badges cost £10 and are usually valid for up to 3 years.

programmes.name_en: Older Person's Free Bus Pass (ENCTS, England)
programmes.funder: Department for Transport / local councils (English National Concessionary Travel Scheme)
programmes.amount_note: Free off-peak bus travel anywhere in England (after 9.30am weekdays, any time weekends and bank holidays) for people of State Pension age

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to your local council (online or paper form)

documents_required.doc: Proof of age
Proof of address
Passport-style photo

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; eligible from State Pension age

programmes.source_snippet: In England you can get a bus pass for free travel when you reach the State Pension age, under the English National Concessionary Travel Scheme; apply to your local council.

programmes.name_en: Disabled Person's Free Bus Pass (ENCTS, England)
programmes.funder: Department for Transport / local councils (English National Concessionary Travel Scheme)
programmes.amount_note: Free off-peak bus travel anywhere in England for eligible disabled people (7 statutory disability categories); some councils offer extra local concessions

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to your local council with evidence of your disability

documents_required.doc: Evidence of disability (e.g. PIP/DLA award, CVI, medical evidence)
Proof of address
Passport-style photo

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; based on statutory disability categories such as severely sight impaired, unable to walk long-term, or ineligible for a driving licence on medical grounds

programmes.source_snippet: A concessionary free bus pass allows eligible disabled residents to travel on buses for free, anywhere in England, valid between 9.30am and 11pm Monday to Friday and at any time on weekends and public holidays.

programmes.amount_note: Free travel on buses, Tube, trams, DLR, London Overground and most National Rail services in London for older and eligible disabled Londoners

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or by paper form to London Councils

documents_required.doc: Proof of age or disability
Proof of London address
Passport-style photo

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; older person's pass from State Pension age, disabled person's pass for eligible London residents

programmes.source_snippet: The Freedom Pass gives free travel across London and free bus journeys nationally to older and disabled people who are resident in a London borough.

programmes.name_en: National Entitlement Card free bus travel (Scotland)
programmes.amount_note: Free bus travel throughout Scotland for everyone aged 60+, eligible disabled people, and all 5-21 year olds (Young Persons' Free Bus Travel Scheme)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for a National Entitlement Card via your local council or getyournec.scot

documents_required.doc: Proof of age or disability
Proof of address in Scotland
Photo

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; universal for under-22s and 60+, plus eligible disabled people

programmes.source_snippet: The National Entitlement Card gives free bus travel across Scotland to people aged 60 and over, eligible disabled people, and all young people aged 5 to 21.

programmes.amount_note: About £30 a year (or £70 for 3 years) for 1/3 off most rail fares across Britain for people aged 16-25 and full-time students of any age

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; full-time students over 25 also eligible

programmes.source_snippet: A 16-25 Railcard gets you 1/3 off rail fares to travel across Britain for just £30 a year, for anyone aged 16-25 or a mature student in full-time study.

programmes.amount_note: About £30 a year (or £70 for 3 years) for 1/3 off most rail fares for people aged 60 and over

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested

programmes.source_snippet: The Senior Railcard gives everyone aged 60 and over 1/3 off Standard and First Class Anytime, Off-Peak and Advance fares across Britain.

programmes.amount_note: About £20 a year (or £54 for 3 years) for 1/3 off rail fares for the cardholder and one accompanying adult

eligibility.income_note: For people who get certain disability benefits (e.g. PIP, DLA), are registered deaf or use a wheelchair, or meet other listed criteria

programmes.source_snippet: The Disabled Persons Railcard allows you and an adult companion to get 1/3 off rail fares across Britain; it costs £20 for one year.

programmes.amount_note: About £30 a year for 1/3 off most rail fares when the two named cardholders travel together

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; any two named people aged 16+ travelling together

programmes.source_snippet: The Two Together Railcard saves two named people 1/3 off rail fares when they travel together, for £30 a year.

programmes.amount_note: About £30 a year for 1/3 off most off-peak rail fares in the Network Railcard area (London and the South East) for the holder and up to 3 accompanying adults

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; anyone aged 16+

programmes.source_snippet: The Network Railcard gives 1/3 off most rail fares for journeys in the Network Railcard area of London and the South East, for £30 a year.

programmes.funder: Motability Operations (overseen by the Motability Foundation)
programmes.amount_note: Lease a car, wheelchair accessible vehicle, scooter or powered wheelchair using the enhanced/higher rate mobility component of PIP, ADP, DLA or equivalent; package includes insurance, servicing and breakdown cover

procedure_steps.detail: Check you receive a qualifying mobility allowance with at least 12 months left
Visit a Motability dealer and order your vehicle

eligibility.income_note: Lease scheme for people receiving the enhanced/higher-rate mobility component of PIP, DLA, ADP or CDP, or armed-forces mobility payments; a qualifying disability benefit, not an income ceiling, is the criterion.

programmes.source_snippet: The Motability Scheme enables disabled people to exchange their qualifying mobility allowance to lease a new car, scooter or powered wheelchair, with insurance, maintenance and breakdown cover included.

programmes.amount_note: Grant of up to £30,000 in England (£36,000 in Wales, £25,000 in Northern Ireland) for essential home adaptations such as ramps, stairlifts and level-access showers; means-tested for adults, not for children

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your council, usually via an occupational therapist assessment of needs
Council approves the adaptation and grant; work is carried out

documents_required.doc: Occupational therapist assessment
Proof of income and savings (adults)

eligibility.income_note: Up to £30,000 (England) for home adaptations; means-tested on the applicant's income and savings above £6,000 against a notional loan amount — under-18s' cases are exempt from the test. No single published ceiling; the means test scales the required contribution.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum grant in England is £30,000; you can apply if you are a homeowner, tenant, or landlord applying on behalf of a tenant, or a disabled person who plans to live in the property.

programmes.amount_note: Loan (repayable with interest when the home is sold) towards mortgage interest for homeowners on Universal Credit, Pension Credit and other means-tested benefits

eligibility.income_note: Loan (not benefit) paying mortgage interest for claimants of UC (after 3 months), Pension Credit, Income Support or income-based JSA/ESA; the qualifying-benefit rule is the means test.

programmes.source_snippet: Support for Mortgage Interest is a loan to help towards interest payments on your mortgage or loans taken out for certain repairs and improvements to your home.

programmes.amount_note: Free or subsidised legal advice, family mediation and representation in court/tribunals for people who cannot afford it and whose case qualifies

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility on GOV.UK and find a legal aid solicitor or adviser

documents_required.doc: Evidence of income, benefits and capital

eligibility.income_note: Civil legal aid (England & Wales, Keycard April 2026): gross monthly income must be £2,657 or less (x12 = £31,884/yr; +£222/month per child beyond the fourth) and disposable income £733 or less per month; disposable capital under £8,000. UC and income-based JSA/ESA/Income Support/Pension Credit GC passport the income test. Scotland and NI run separate schemes.

programmes.source_snippet: You could get legal aid to help pay for legal advice, family mediation and representation in a court or tribunal if you cannot afford to pay and your case is serious enough.

programmes.amount_note: Save up to £50 a month for 4 years and get a 50% government bonus on the highest balance, worth up to £1,200 in total

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and open an account online via GOV.UK with a Government Gateway account

eligibility.income_note: Minimum-earnings rule, not a maximum: from April 2025 open to anyone on Universal Credit with earned income of at least £1 in the last monthly assessment period (previously Working Tax Credit claimants too). Save up to £50/month; 50% government bonus over 4 years (max £1,200).

programmes.source_snippet: Customers are able to save up to £50 per calendar month in their Help to Save account for up to 48 calendar months; after 2 years the Government awards a 50% bonus of the highest balance saved.

programmes.funder: HM Treasury (offered by banks and building societies)
programmes.amount_note: Government adds a 25% bonus to savings up to £4,000 a year (max £1,000 bonus a year) for first-time home purchase (up to £450,000) or retirement from age 60; open ages 18-39

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; 25% withdrawal charge applies if used for anything other than a first home, retirement at 60+, or terminal illness

programmes.source_snippet: With a Lifetime ISA you can save up to £4,000 each year until you're 50, and the government will add a 25% bonus to your savings, up to a maximum of £1,000 per year.

programmes.amount_note: Transfer £1,260 of unused Personal Allowance to a spouse or civil partner, saving up to £252 in tax each year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via GOV.UK; can be backdated up to 4 tax years

eligibility.income_note: Lets a non-taxpayer transfer £1,260 of Personal Allowance to a spouse/civil partner paying basic-rate tax: the lower earner must have income below the £12,570 Personal Allowance and the higher earner's income must be between £12,571 and £50,270 (2025/26); worth up to £252/yr.

programmes.source_snippet: Marriage Allowance lets you transfer £1,260 of your Personal Allowance to your husband, wife or civil partner, reducing their tax by up to £252 in the tax year.

programmes.amount_note: Extra tax-free allowance (£3,070 in 2025/26) added to the Personal Allowance for people registered blind or severely sight impaired

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; can be transferred to a spouse/civil partner if unused

programmes.source_snippet: Blind Person's Allowance is an extra amount of tax-free allowance added to your Personal Allowance if you're registered blind or severely sight impaired.

programmes.amount_note: Government-backed personal loans of £500 to £25,000 at a fixed 6% interest over 1-5 years to start or grow a business, with free mentoring and business support

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via the Start Up Loans website and work with a delivery partner on your business plan

documents_required.doc: Business plan and cash flow forecast
Proof of identity

eligibility.income_note: For people aged 18+ starting or running a UK-based business trading for less than 36 months; credit checks apply

programmes.source_snippet: Start Up Loans is a government-backed scheme helping people start or grow a business in the UK, offering loans of up to £25,000 with free support and mentoring.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 39 weeks of payments for pregnant people who do not qualify for Statutory Maternity Pay (e.g. self-employed or recently stopped work); paid at a standard weekly rate or 90% of average earnings if lower

procedure_steps.detail: Send form MA1 with proof of pregnancy (MAT B1) and earnings evidence

documents_required.doc: MAT B1 certificate
Payslips or self-employment evidence

eligibility.income_note: For those who do not qualify for Statutory Maternity Pay: requires employment/self-employment in 26 of the 66 test weeks with earnings of at least £30/week in 13 weeks; pays £187.18/week (2025/26) or 90% of average earnings if lower.

programmes.source_snippet: You could get Maternity Allowance for up to 39 weeks if you're pregnant or have recently given birth and don't qualify for Statutory Maternity Pay.

programmes.amount_note: 39 weeks: 90% of average weekly earnings for the first 6 weeks, then the lower of 90% of earnings or the standard weekly rate for 33 weeks

procedure_steps.detail: Tell your employer and give them your MAT B1 certificate at least 15 weeks before the baby is due

documents_required.doc: MAT B1 certificate from midwife or doctor

eligibility.income_note: Must have worked for the employer for 26 weeks by the qualifying week and earn at least the Lower Earnings Limit

programmes.source_snippet: Statutory Maternity Pay is paid for up to 39 weeks: 90% of your average weekly earnings for the first 6 weeks, then the standard rate or 90% of earnings (whichever is lower) for the next 33 weeks.

programmes.amount_note: 1 or 2 weeks of leave paid at the standard weekly rate or 90% of average weekly earnings (whichever is lower) after the birth or adoption of a child

eligibility.income_note: Must meet continuous employment and minimum earnings conditions

programmes.source_snippet: When you take time off because your partner is having a baby, adopting a child or having a baby through surrogacy, you might be eligible for 1 or 2 weeks of Statutory Paternity Pay and Leave.

programmes.name_en: Statutory Shared Parental Pay and Leave
programmes.amount_note: Parents can share up to 50 weeks of leave and 37 weeks of pay (at the standard weekly rate or 90% of earnings, whichever is lower) in the first year after birth or adoption

eligibility.income_note: Both parents must meet employment and earnings tests; the mother must curtail maternity leave/pay

programmes.source_snippet: You and your partner may be able to get Shared Parental Leave and Statutory Shared Parental Pay if you're having a baby or adopting a child.

programmes.amount_note: A lump sum followed by up to 18 monthly payments, at a higher rate for those with dependent children and a standard rate otherwise, when a spouse, civil partner or cohabiting partner dies

procedure_steps.detail: Claim online, by phone or by post within 3 months of the death for the full amount

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; depends on the deceased's National Insurance contributions

programmes.source_snippet: You may be able to get Bereavement Support Payment if your husband, wife, civil partner or partner you lived with has died; it consists of a first payment followed by up to 18 monthly payments.

programmes.amount_note: Covers necessary funeral costs (burial/cremation fees) plus up to £1,000 for other expenses such as the coffin or funeral director's fees, for people on qualifying benefits

procedure_steps.detail: Claim within 6 months of the funeral, by phone or form SF200

eligibility.income_note: Covers cremation/burial fees plus up to £1,000 of other costs for people arranging a funeral who receive UC, Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit, tax credits or a Sure Start Maternity Grant; the qualifying-benefit rule is the means test.

programmes.source_snippet: You could get a Funeral Expenses Payment if you get certain benefits and need help to pay for a funeral you're arranging; Scotland has the Funeral Support Payment instead.

programmes.amount_note: Weekly tax-free payment for people bringing up a child whose parents have died (or in some cases where one parent has died and the other cannot be traced or is in prison)

eligibility.income_note: £22.10/week (2025/26) for people bringing up a child whose parents have died (with Child Benefit entitlement); not means-tested.

programmes.source_snippet: You could get Guardian's Allowance if you're bringing up a child whose parents have died; it's paid weekly and is tax-free.

programmes.amount_note: Free TV licence for people aged 75 or over who receive Pension Credit; 50% discount for people registered blind or severely sight impaired; reduced fee for care home residents

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to TV Licensing with proof of Pension Credit or sight impairment

documents_required.doc: Proof of Pension Credit award or Certificate of Visual Impairment

eligibility.income_note: Free licence for over-75s receiving Pension Credit; 50% discount for registered blind people; £7.50 ARC licence for care-home residents. The Pension Credit requirement is the income-linked test for the free over-75 licence.

programmes.source_snippet: If you're 75 or over and you or your partner receive Pension Credit, you can get a free TV licence; if you're blind (severely sight impaired) you can get a 50% concession.

programmes.amount_note: Low-cost fibre broadband and calls packages for customers on Universal Credit, Pension Credit and other means-tested benefits, at a fraction of standard prices with no exit fees

eligibility.income_note: Social tariff (~£15/month, 36Mbps) for customers on Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA (or PIP for the phone-only plan); eligibility verified with DWP — the benefit test is the published rule.

programmes.source_snippet: BT Home Essentials is a low-cost broadband and phone plan for customers on Universal Credit and other means-tested benefits.

programmes.name_en: Virgin Media Essential Broadband social tariff
programmes.amount_note: Discounted broadband-only package for people receiving Universal Credit and other qualifying benefits, with no fixed-term contract and no price rises while on benefits

eligibility.income_note: Social tariff (£12.50/month, 15Mbps; Essential Plus 54Mbps ~£20) for Universal Credit claimants; eligibility verified electronically with DWP.

programmes.source_snippet: Essential broadband is Virgin Media's social tariff: low-cost broadband for customers receiving Universal Credit and certain other benefits.

programmes.amount_note: Heavily discounted SIM-only mobile plan for people receiving means-tested benefits, offering unlimited 5G data, calls and texts at a low monthly price

eligibility.income_note: Vodafone mobile social tariff (£10/month unlimited 5G data, calls and texts) for people on Jobseeker's Allowance, Universal Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, Disability Allowance or Personal Independence Payment.

programmes.source_snippet: VOXI For Now is a discounted mobile plan giving unlimited data, minutes and texts at a low monthly price to people receiving government benefits.

programmes.amount_note: Discounted broadband for existing Sky customers who receive Universal Credit or Pension Credit, on a rolling monthly contract

eligibility.income_note: Social tariff (£20/month, 36Mbps) for Sky broadband customers (and DWP-verified eligible NOW Broadband customers) receiving Universal Credit or Pension Credit.

programmes.source_snippet: Sky Broadband Basics is a lower-cost broadband tariff available to Sky customers who claim Universal Credit or Pension Credit.

programmes.amount_note: Caps the water bill of metered households on certain benefits who use a lot of water for essential reasons (3+ children or a medical condition), so they pay no more than the average metered bill

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to your water company with evidence of benefits and water use need

documents_required.doc: Proof of qualifying benefits
Medical evidence or proof of 3+ children in the household

eligibility.income_note: Caps metered water bills at the company average for households on a means-tested benefit (or UC) that either have 3+ children under 19 or a medical condition requiring extra water use; the benefit test is the published rule.

programmes.source_snippet: WaterSure caps the bills of water meter customers on certain benefits who need to use a lot of water because of a medical condition or because they have three or more children.

programmes.funder: Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) via local councils
programmes.amount_note: Council-delivered help with food, energy and essential costs for vulnerable households; the type of support (vouchers, grants, cash) and criteria vary by council

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your local council to ask what Household Support Fund help is available

eligibility.income_note: DWP-funded council crisis support (food, energy, essentials); each English council sets its own eligibility, usually targeting low-income households not captured by benefit criteria — thresholds vary locally.

programmes.source_snippet: The Household Support Fund provides funding to local councils in England to help vulnerable households with the cost of essentials such as food and energy bills.

programmes.name_en: Local Welfare Assistance / crisis support schemes
programmes.amount_note: Emergency grants, vouchers or goods from your council for people in crisis (e.g. after a disaster or when unable to afford food or essentials); names and rules differ by council

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your local council and ask about local welfare or crisis support

eligibility.income_note: Discretionary council-run crisis grants/loans (e.g. emergency food, fuel, white goods); locally means-assessed with no national threshold — availability and criteria vary by council.

programmes.source_snippet: Local welfare assistance schemes are run by councils to help people in an emergency or crisis who cannot afford essentials such as food, heating or clothing.

programmes.funder: Turn2us (national charity) and partner grant-giving charities
programmes.amount_note: Searchable database of thousands of charitable funds offering grants to people in financial hardship based on occupation, health, location and circumstances

procedure_steps.detail: Use the Turn2us grants search to find funds matching your circumstances
Apply directly to each charitable fund with its own form

eligibility.income_note: Grant-search charity: thousands of charitable funds each set their own means tests, often linked to low income, occupation, health or location; no single income ceiling.

programmes.source_snippet: Turn2us is a national charity that helps people in financial hardship access welfare benefits and charitable grants through its benefits calculator and grants search.

programmes.amount_note: One-off payment to help with the costs of starting a new job (travel, clothing, childcare) for people in Scotland aged 16-24 (or care leavers up to 25) who have been out of paid work on qualifying benefits

eligibility.income_note: £314.70 one-off (£503.55 with children) for 16-24 year olds (or care leavers to 25) in Scotland who were on a qualifying low-income benefit for 6+ months and start a job; the benefit-history rule is the means test.

programmes.source_snippet: Job Start Payment is a one-off payment to help young people in Scotland with the costs of starting a new job after a period out of work on qualifying benefits.

programmes.amount_note: Fibre 2 Essentials at £20/month (up to 73Mbps); the earlier £12 Fibre 1 Essentials tier was withdrawn in 2026

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and apply on Vodafone's social tariffs page
Provide National Insurance number for automatic DWP eligibility verification

documents_required.doc: National Insurance number (for DWP benefit verification)

eligibility.income_note: For new and existing customers receiving Universal Credit, Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, Income Support, Reduced Earnings Allowance, Personal Independence Payment or Disability Living Allowance; the qualifying-benefit rule is the means test.

programmes.source_snippet: Vodafone Essentials Broadband is available to new and existing customers receiving Jobseeker's Allowance, Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Employment Support Allowance, Income Support, Reduced Earnings Allowance, Personal Independence Payment or Disability Allowance.

programmes.amount_note: Unlimited data, calls and texts from £10/month for people on qualifying benefits

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via O2 and complete the benefit eligibility check (DWP verification)

documents_required.doc: National Insurance number for benefit verification

eligibility.income_note: Mobile social tariff for people receiving means-tested benefits such as Universal Credit; eligibility verified via the DWP — the benefit test is the published rule.

programmes.source_snippet: O2 Essential Plan: mobile social tariff offering unlimited data from £10 a month for customers on qualifying benefits.

programmes.amount_note: 50% discount on the water bill for eligible low-income households; London pilot auto-enrols households whose bill exceeds 5% of equivalised net income

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via Thames Water's financial support page or contact the Extra Care team
Complete the income and expenditure assessment

documents_required.doc: Details of household income and benefits

eligibility.income_note: Water poverty test: household qualifies where the water bill exceeds about 5% of net income after housing costs and disability benefits (thresholds previously published as £17,005 Thames Valley / £21,749 London, now assessed case-by-case). Discount between 25% and 99%, typically 50%.

programmes.source_snippet: Customers whose water bill is more than five per cent of their equivalised net income could qualify for a 50 per cent discount under Thames Water's WaterHelp scheme.

programmes.name_local: Big Difference Scheme (Severn Trent social tariff)
programmes.name_en: Big Difference Scheme (Severn Trent social tariff)
programmes.amount_note: Reduced water bill via an assessed payment plan (minimum discount around £117, up to about £764); runs 12 months then re-apply

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to Severn Trent directly or via a debt advice agency such as Citizens Advice
Household income assessment determines the discount band

documents_required.doc: Proof of household income

eligibility.income_note: For Severn Trent customers with household income below £24,454 a year (households with child dependants may qualify with an additional income allowance); assessed annually.

programmes.source_snippet: The Big Difference Scheme is for household income of less than £24,454 (households with child dependants may be eligible for an additional income allowance in excess of this).

programmes.name_local: Back on Track (United Utilities social tariff)
programmes.name_en: Back on Track (United Utilities social tariff)
programmes.amount_note: Water bill reduced to a lower capped amount for the year depending on circumstances

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via United Utilities with evidence of benefits or reduced income

documents_required.doc: Evidence of income-related benefits or reduced household income

eligibility.income_note: For customers on income-related benefits (UC, tax credits, Housing Benefit, Council Tax Support, Pension Credit etc.) who are in arrears, or whose household income is under £21,500 a year following a recent life event (job loss, bereavement, illness).

programmes.source_snippet: To be eligible for the Back on Track scheme you must receive at least one income-related benefit and be in arrears, or have a household income of less than £21,500 a year due to a recent life event.

programmes.name_local: Scottish Welfare Fund (Crisis Grants and Community Care Grants)
programmes.name_en: Scottish Welfare Fund (Crisis Grants and Community Care Grants)
programmes.amount_note: Discretionary, non-repayable grants; Crisis Grants cover emergencies (food, heating, essentials), Community Care Grants help people establish or maintain a settled home

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through your local council (online, phone or in person)
Council assesses priority level; crisis decisions within 2 working days, community care within 15 working days

documents_required.doc: Details of the crisis or items needed and financial circumstances

eligibility.income_note: For people aged 16+ on a low income — you do not need to be receiving benefits; councils assess income, savings and vulnerability case-by-case. No single published income ceiling.

programmes.source_snippet: Community Care Grants and Crisis Grants do not have to be paid back; you apply through your local council and must be over 16 and on a low income.

programmes.amount_note: Non-repayable grants: Emergency Assistance Payment for a crisis (food, gas, electricity, clothing, emergency travel) and Individual Assistance Payment for essential household items to live independently

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via GOV.WALES or by phone
Assessor reviews need; emergency applications are prioritised

documents_required.doc: Details of the crisis and financial situation

eligibility.income_note: Open to people ordinarily resident in Wales in extreme financial hardship or crisis; no formal income threshold but circumstances and savings are assessed. You do not need to be on benefits.

programmes.source_snippet: The Discretionary Assistance Fund provides two types of grant that you do not need to pay back: the Emergency Assistance Payment and the Individual Assistance Payment.

programmes.amount_note: Short-term grants or interest-free loans for a crisis that places health, safety or wellbeing at significant risk (living expenses, household items, rent in advance)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via nidirect or by phone to the Discretionary Support service
Decision maker assesses whether the situation qualifies and whether award is a grant or loan

documents_required.doc: Details of crisis, income and savings

eligibility.income_note: For NI residents facing an extreme, exceptional or crisis situation; annual income must not exceed the published Discretionary Support threshold (broadly aligned to means-tested benefit levels); assessed case-by-case.

programmes.source_snippet: Discretionary Support is short-term financial help for people in Northern Ireland in a crisis which places their or their family's health, safety or wellbeing at significant risk.

programmes.amount_note: Automatic mitigation payments covering losses from the Benefit Cap, Social Sector Size Criteria ('bedroom tax'), ESA/PIP transition and loss of disability premiums; extended to end of March 2028
programmes.deadline_note: Most schemes extended to 31 March 2028 under 2024 Executive decision

procedure_steps.detail: No claim needed — the Department for Communities identifies and pays eligible households automatically

documents_required.doc: None (paid automatically to affected benefit claimants)

eligibility.income_note: Paid to households losing out under welfare changes (Benefit Cap, bedroom tax, PIP/ESA transitions); the underlying means-tested benefit is the income test. Over 38,000 recipients in 2023/24.

programmes.source_snippet: Welfare Supplementary Payment schemes will continue in payment after agreement by the Executive; most of the payments will run until the end of March 2028.

programmes.amount_note: Free school lunch for every primary school pupil (Reception to Year 6), worth roughly £500-£650 per child per year; no means test

procedure_steps.detail: Automatic for all children in maintained primary schools in Wales — no application needed

documents_required.doc: None

eligibility.income_note: Universal — no income test. (For secondary pupils in Wales, benefits-based eligibility still applies, including a £7,400 net earnings limit for UC households.)

programmes.source_snippet: All primary school children in Wales can now access Universal Primary Free School Meals, rolled out between September 2022 and September 2024.

programmes.amount_note: 12.5 hours/week of funded part-time childcare for 2-year-olds (39 weeks/year), plus enhanced health visiting, parenting support and speech & language support; being rolled out to all 2-year-olds in Wales area by area

procedure_steps.detail: Check whether your area is covered via your local Family Information Service
Register with a Flying Start childcare setting from the term after your child's 2nd birthday

documents_required.doc: Proof of address and child's date of birth

eligibility.income_note: Area-based, not means-tested: all 2-year-olds in designated Flying Start areas (initially the most disadvantaged communities) qualify; full roll-out achieved in Merthyr Tydfil, Newport, Swansea and Wrexham, expanding elsewhere.

programmes.source_snippet: 12.5 hours of Flying Start childcare is gradually being made available to all 2 year olds across Wales starting with the most disadvantaged areas first.

programmes.name_local: Childcare Offer for Wales (30 hours for 3-4 year olds)
programmes.amount_note: Up to 30 hours/week of funded early education and childcare for eligible working parents of 3-4 year olds, for up to 48 weeks a year (10 hours Foundation Phase nursery + up to 20 hours childcare)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via your local authority Family Information Service
Receive a Childcare Offer code and give it to your registered provider
Reconfirm eligibility every 3 months

documents_required.doc: National Insurance number and employment details
Child's birth certificate and proof of address in Wales

eligibility.income_note: Each parent must earn at least the equivalent of 16 hours/week at National Minimum Wage and neither parent may have gross income over £100,000 per year (per-parent cap); some students, kinship carers and newly self-employed parents also qualify.

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible working parents of three and four year olds in Wales can access up to 30 hours per week of government-funded early education and childcare, with a £100,000 gross income cap per parent.

programmes.funder: Department for Work and Pensions / National Rail
programmes.amount_note: 50% discount on selected rail tickets (Anytime Day, Off-Peak Day and season tickets up to 3 months); also 50% off some bus/tram fares in participating areas and Oyster season tickets in London

procedure_steps.detail: Ask your Work Coach at your local Jobcentre Plus to issue the card

documents_required.doc: Evidence of benefit claim duration

eligibility.income_note: For people claiming Jobseeker's Allowance or Universal Credit for 3-9 months (aged 18-24) or 3-12 months (aged 25+); other benefit recipients engaged with a Jobcentre adviser may qualify from 3 months. Benefit status, not an income figure, is the test.

programmes.source_snippet: The card is provided to those claiming Jobseekers Allowance or Universal Credit for 3 to 9 months (for 18 to 24 year olds) or 3 to 12 months (for over 25s), and entitles you to a 50% discount on selected rail tickets.

programmes.name_local: Young Persons' (Under 22s) Free Bus Travel Scheme (Scotland)
programmes.name_en: Young Persons' Free Bus Travel (Scotland, under 22)
programmes.amount_note: Free travel on most registered bus services across Scotland for 5-21 year olds with a National Entitlement Card or Young Scot NEC

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for an NEC or Young Scot NEC online at getyournec.scot or via your local council (parents apply for 5-15s)

documents_required.doc: Proof of age and Scottish residence
Photo (for cards for those aged 11+)

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested — all Scotland residents aged 5-21 qualify (under-5s already travel free).

programmes.source_snippet: Young people aged 5 to 21 who live in Scotland can get a free bus pass. You can use this on most bus services in Scotland.

programmes.name_local: Welsh Concessionary Travel Card (60+ and disabled)
programmes.amount_note: Free travel at any time on local bus services throughout Wales for people aged 60+ and eligible disabled people; discounted or free travel on some rail services (e.g. 34% off Cardiff & Valleys lines)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via the Transport for Wales portal (or by post)
Upload proof of date of birth, two proofs of address, a photo and National Insurance number

documents_required.doc: Proof of date of birth
Two proofs of address in Wales
Passport-style photo and National Insurance number

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested: available to Wales residents aged 60 and over, eligible disabled people and injured service personnel.

programmes.source_snippet: If your primary address is in Wales and you're either aged 60 and over or meet the Government's disability eligibility criteria, you can travel for free on most bus services in Wales and the borders.

programmes.funder: Transport for London / Mayor of London
programmes.amount_note: Free travel on bus, Tube, tram, DLR, London Overground, Elizabeth line and most National Rail services in London (weekdays except 04:30-09:00; anytime weekends); £20 admin fee, annual address check

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online with a TfL account
Provide photo, proof of age/address and pay the £20 fee

documents_required.doc: Proof of age and London borough address
Digital photo and debit/credit card for the £20 fee

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested: for London borough residents aged 60 or over who are not yet eligible for a Freedom Pass (State Pension age).

programmes.source_snippet: If you're 60 or over and live in a London borough, you can get a 60+ London Oyster photocard until you're eligible for a Freedom Pass.

programmes.amount_note: £30 a year (or until your 18th birthday) for 50% off most rail fares, including season tickets

procedure_steps.detail: Buy online with proof of age

documents_required.doc: Proof of age (passport, driving licence or birth certificate)

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested — a paid discount card available to all 16 and 17 year olds.

programmes.source_snippet: The 16-17 Saver costs £30 and gives 50% off most rail fares for 16 and 17 year olds, including season tickets.

programmes.amount_note: Free, flexible courses of up to 16 weeks in priority sectors (digital, construction, green skills, HGV driving, health) with a guaranteed employer interview on completion; employers contribute 10-30% when upskilling their own staff
programmes.deadline_note: Funded through the National Skills Fund; course availability varies by region and funding round

procedure_steps.detail: Find a Skills Bootcamp via GOV.UK or the National Careers Service
Apply direct to the training provider; check local eligibility criteria

documents_required.doc: Proof of age, UK residency and right to work

eligibility.income_note: Free to independent learners aged 19+ whether in work, self-employed or unemployed — no income test; some courses are postcode-restricted to the funding region.

programmes.source_snippet: Skills Bootcamps are free, flexible courses of up to 16 weeks that help you develop new skills and fast-track to a job interview or gain new responsibilities with your current employer.

programmes.name_local: Free Courses for Jobs (level 3 offer, England)
programmes.amount_note: Fully funded level 3 qualification (A-level equivalent) in sectors such as accounting, digital, health and social care and construction; course length a few weeks to a year

procedure_steps.detail: Check the list of eligible level 3 qualifications and providers on GOV.UK
Enrol with the training provider; ask about help with childcare/travel costs

documents_required.doc: Proof of age, residency and prior qualifications/earnings

eligibility.income_note: Free if you are 19+, live in England and either do not already have a level 3 qualification, or earn less than £25,750 a year / are unemployed (National Living Wage-linked threshold).

programmes.source_snippet: The government will pay for you to do a course if you're 19 or older and you either: earn less than £25,750; are not in work.

programmes.amount_note: Voluntary supported employment programme (individual placement and support) for disabled people, people with health conditions and other disadvantaged groups; rolling out across England and Wales from 2025 with funding to 2030

procedure_steps.detail: Self-refer or get referred via a Work Coach, local authority or partner organisation

documents_required.doc: Varies by local delivery body

eligibility.income_note: Voluntary programme for disabled people, those with health conditions or complex barriers (e.g. care leavers, homeless people, veterans); no income test — eligibility is based on disadvantage and being out of work or at risk of losing work.

programmes.source_snippet: Connect to Work is a DWP-funded voluntary supported employment programme available across England and Wales for disabled and disadvantaged people.

programmes.funder: British Business Bank (for the Secretary of State for Business and Trade)
programmes.amount_note: 70% government-backed guarantee to lenders on SME finance: term loans, overdrafts, asset finance, invoice finance and asset-based lending from £25,001 (term loans/overdrafts; from £1,000 for asset/invoice finance) up to £2m (£1m for NI Protocol-scope borrowers); extended to March 2030

procedure_steps.detail: Approach an accredited lender (list on the British Business Bank site)
Lender applies its normal credit checks and applies the 70% government guarantee

documents_required.doc: Business accounts and trading history
Business plan and affordability evidence

eligibility.income_note: For UK businesses with annual turnover up to £45m (rising to £54m under announced enhancements) generating over 50% of turnover from trading; not a household income test — the guarantee goes to the lender and the borrower remains 100% liable.

programmes.source_snippet: The Growth Guarantee Scheme is the successor to the Recovery Loan Scheme and can generally support facility sizes of up to £2m, providing the lender with a 70% government-backed guarantee.

programmes.name_local: Flat Rate Expenses tax relief (uniform and work clothing)
programmes.amount_note: Tax relief on a fixed annual allowance (typically £6-£140 depending on occupation, e.g. £60 for many manual trades) for cleaning, repairing or replacing work uniforms and tools; claim back to HMRC for up to 4 tax years

procedure_steps.detail: Check if your occupation is on HMRC's flat rate expenses list
Claim online via HMRC (P87 or Self Assessment), or by phone/post

documents_required.doc: National Insurance number and employment details

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested: available to employees whose job requires them to maintain uniform or tools their employer does not pay for; relief is worth 20-45% of the flat-rate amount depending on your tax band.

programmes.source_snippet: You may be able to claim tax relief if you use your own money for things you must buy for your job, including repairing or replacing small tools and cleaning, repairing or replacing specialist clothing.

programmes.name_local: Family Fund grants (disabled or seriously ill children)
programmes.amount_note: Grants for essential items (washing machines, beds, clothing, sensory/play equipment, family breaks) for families raising disabled or seriously ill children and young people

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and apply via the Family Fund online application form
Upload supporting documents (benefit award letter or payslips, disability evidence)

documents_required.doc: Recent benefit award letter or last 3 months of payslips
Evidence of the child's condition (EHCP, professional reports, supporting letter)

eligibility.income_note: Means-assessed: Family Fund looks at household income and the impact of disability; open to low-income families and those receiving benefits, resident in the UK for at least 6 months. No single published national ceiling is stated publicly — income is assessed in the round.

programmes.source_snippet: Family Fund looks at your income and the impact of disability on your child; you can apply if you are the parent/carer of a child or young person with a disability or serious illness and are on a low income or receiving benefits.

programmes.amount_note: Free NHS prescriptions and free NHS dental treatment while pregnant and for 12 months after the birth; certificate backdated to one month before application and valid until 12 months after due date/birth

procedure_steps.detail: Ask your midwife, doctor or health visitor to apply on your behalf (digital service gives the certificate by email immediately)

documents_required.doc: Application completed by a healthcare professional
documents_required.note: Claiming without a valid certificate risks a £100 penalty charge

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested — entitlement is based on pregnancy or having given birth in the last 12 months (including after miscarriage or stillbirth).

programmes.source_snippet: You're entitled to a maternity exemption certificate if, at the time of your application, you are pregnant or have given birth in the last 12 months.

programmes.name_local: Free NHS wigs and fabric supports
programmes.name_en: NHS wigs and fabric supports (help with charges)
programmes.amount_note: Free (or reduced-cost) wigs and fabric supports for exempt groups; otherwise charges apply in England (e.g. stock modacrylic wig £80.15, full bespoke human hair wig £310.55, surgical bra £32.50, abdominal/spinal support £49.05); free to all in Scotland and Wales via hospitals

procedure_steps.detail: Tell the hospital fitter you are entitled to free provision and show proof of exemption or an HC2/HC3 certificate
If you have paid, claim a refund with form HC5(W) within 3 months

documents_required.doc: Proof of qualifying benefit, HC2 certificate, or war pension exemption certificate

eligibility.income_note: Free in England for under-16s (under-19 in FTE), hospital inpatients, war pensioners (accepted disablement), and recipients of Income Support, income-based JSA/ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit, UC within the earnings criteria, or HC2 certificate holders; HC3 gives partial help via the NHS Low Income Scheme (capital limit £16,000).

programmes.source_snippet: You can get free wigs and fabric supports if you are under 16, 16 to 18 and in full-time education, a hospital inpatient, a war pensioner, or receiving qualifying benefits or named on a valid HC2 certificate.
